messages:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert triggered — high rate of container restarts on pool rtx-usw2-3 due to repeated GPU OOM during prefill. error rate 45% over last 3m. paging oncall @Samir and @Lee
Samir: oncall here, looking
Lee: I'm awake, grabbing metrics and logs, what's the customer impact?
Incident Bot: Affected tenant: acme-retail-prod. ~12% of their requests are failing with container restart (SIGKILL) during prefill for long-context prompts (>120k tokens).
Samir: I can repro locally with a long-system-prompt test — prefill allocation hits peak memory then CUDA driver reset.
Samir: paste logs:
```
[2026-03-15 02:12:23] ERR runtime: prefill alloc 14.7GB failed, cudaErrorIllegalAddress -> GPU reset
[2026-03-15 02:12:24] WARN container: restarting due to non-zero exit (137)
```
Lee: hmm, illegal address then reset. Could be memory fragmentation + very large batch. Any noisy neighbor? OpsBot, can you show node allocation for that pool?
OpsBot: rtx-usw2-3 nodes: 8 total, 6 active pods for acme-retail-prod, average GPU mem used 78% baseline, spike to 102% on prefill windows. No explicit OOMkilled by kernel; container exited due to runtime SIGKILL.
Maria: customer impact from CS: acme reports elevated error rate and some timeouts in checkout flows. They're seeing 500s. We need ETA and customer comms.
Devon: two parallel mitigation tracks: 1) immediate live mitigation so customer stays online, 2) root-cause triage. I’ll lead mitigations.
Samir: immediate idea — apply per-tenant prefill size cap and prefix trimming at the gateway so we avoid building >100k token prefill. Can do a quick routing rule for acme to wire in prefix trim.
Lee: also can throttle concurrent prefill requests for acme to 1 per GPU. That will reduce simultaneous peak allocations.
Devon: @OpsBot, can we move acme traffic to standby pool rtx-usw2-standby (mixed with smaller models) while we patch?
OpsBot: standby has capacity but models there are quantized-cold and may increase latency ~80-120ms. Can shift subset of traffic via smart-routing for canary.
Samir: I'll push a hotpatch to runtime to enable OOM backpressure: if prefill allocation >90% of free mem, return 429 with retry-after instead of letting container attempt the allocation. Small change, canary to 1 node.
Lee: while Samir does that, I'll add a temporary per-tenant prompt-size limiter in the gateway for acme (truncate system prompt to 32k tokens, log truncation event). That should prevent the largest prefill allocations.
Samir: hotpatch applied to canary node (rtx-usw2-3-node-07). monitoring now shows canary rejects ~7% of acme requests with 429, and no container restarts on canary.
Samir: stack trace from canary when 429 path hit:
```
runtime.prefill: calculate_estimated_alloc -> estimated_total = 13.8GB > threshold -> raise PrefillTooLargeError
```
Lee: good sign. OpsBot, route 15% of acme traffic to standby pool for now (non-critical endpoints). Maria, advise CS to route critical checkout requests to primary but we’ll throttle non-essential analytics to standby.
Maria: sending CS note now. email draft: "We've identified prefill OOMs triggered by very large prompts; performing live mitigation (prompt truncation + throttling). Expect partial degradation for heavy prompt workflows. We'll follow up with a patch"
Customer Success: acked, they want us to minimize retries for checkout. Suggest we mark checkout endpoints as high-priority to avoid 429s — can we special-case?
Lee: yes we can add route-level override to bypass prefix-trim for checkout but keep strict concurrency limit. That reduces erroring while protecting system.
Devon: do it. But ensure checkout has a shorter timeout to avoid long retried prefill.
Samir: telemetry update: after applying gateway truncation + canary backpressure, cluster-wide restarts dropped from 45% -> 4% in last 6m. latency impact: +120ms p95 for canary-switched requests.
OpsBot: scheduled a rolling update to apply backpressure change to 2 more nodes in the pool, will not update all nodes until we confirm stability.
Lee: we need a longer-term fix: investigate fragmentation vs allocation strategy, possibly pre-allocating page-aligned pinned buffers or switching to split-prefill allocation. I'll open an RFC and a follow-up issue.
Samir: root-cause notes: long contiguous prefill allocation exceeds available contiguous GPU memory due to fragmentation; CUDA illegal address likely caused by driver reset under stress. Also large single-request allocations are exacerbating it.
Devon: capture next steps for incident report: 1) rollback plan if hotpatch causes issues (we can revert gateway rule and backpressure), 2) patch runtime to fail-fast on over-threshold prefill (Samir), 3) gateway prompt-length enforcement and per-tenant concurrency caps (Lee), 4) routing fallback to standby quantized models for large-context workloads (Ops), 5) customer follow-up and SLA credits assessment (CS).
Maria: CS will send an update to acme in 30m with mitigation summary and expected timeline for permanent fix.
Samir: creating postmortem ticket: INC-7077777 with logs, heap profiles, and canary metrics. Link will be added here.
Incident Bot: :white_check_mark: mitigation showing progress. continuing monitoring. oncall rotation: @Samir stays primary for 2h then handoff to @Lee unless resolved.
Devon: any need to page infra-night for node-drain? OpsBot, do we need to cordon any node?
OpsBot: flagged node rtx-usw2-3-node-03 as 'suspect-fragmentation' — we'll cordon and drain after off-peak (in 45m) to avoid disrupting throughput. No immediate drain.
Samir: I'll keep watch on OOM/Restart graphs. If restarts creep above 10% we'll escalate to SEV.
Maria: CS note posted to customer Slack channel and emailed ops@acme. They replied: "Thanks — please keep checkout unaffected."
Samir: updated canary metrics show stabilization. marking this thread monitored. final handoff note will be posted at 7077777899.
PagerDuty: Incident resolved? Please confirm handoff state.
Lee: handoff accepted, I'll be primary for next shift. Current state: mitigations in place, restart rate 3.8%, customer routed to mixed pool with priority checkout bypass. Working on RFC for allocator changes.
Samir: adding tags: prefill-oom, long-context, customer-impact, hotpatch.
Devon: great. We'll draft postmortem and proposed allocator design (split allocations + fragmentation defrag heuristics).
Maria: CS will follow up with acme and offer credit if necessary.
Incident Bot: thread closed for active paging at 7077777899 — monitoring continues.
